messages.author: 42aeee6b766a85db
messages.subject: Unable to install
parts:
I am following the instructions for installing Stan at https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/wiki/RStan-Getting-Started#prerequisites

I got as far as installing the Rtools package to provide a C++ compiler and that installed successfully

# using library inline to compile a C++ code on the fly
library(inline) 
library(Rcpp)
src <- ' 
  std::vector<std::string> s; 
  s.push_back("hello");
  s.push_back("world");
  return Rcpp::wrap(s);
'
hellofun <- cxxfunction(body = src, includes = '', plugin = 'Rcpp', verbose = FALSE)
cat(hellofun(), ' ') 


I get the following error message

> # using library inline to compile a C++ code on the fly
> library(inline) 
> library(Rcpp)

Attaching package: ‘Rcpp’

The following object is masked from ‘package:inline’:

    registerPlugin

> src <- ' 
+   std::vector<std::string> s; 
+   s.push_back("hello");
+   s.push_back("world");
+   return Rcpp::wrap(s);
+ '
> hellofun <- cxxfunction(body = src, includes = '', plugin = 'Rcpp', verbose = FALSE)
Error in system(cmd, intern = !verbose) : 'C:/Program' not found
> cat(hellofun(), ' ') 
Error in cat(hellofun(), " ") : could not find function "hellofun"

I tried re-installing R with the latest version and then re-installing Rtools and the Rcpp and inlines packages, to no effect.
Does anybody have any idea what could be the problem?

Grateful for any clues.

Blaise F Egan

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Unable to install
parts: This appears to be a problem with spaces in the pathname
Error in system(cmd, intern = !verbose) : 'C:/Program' not found

Although, I thought that wasn't a problem for recent versions of R and Rcpp. You might try it with both R and Rtools installed do a path that has no spaces and no non-ASCII characters.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Unable to install
parts:
I thought Rcpp had finally solved the problem with spaces.

The R FAQ

http://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/rw-FAQ.html#How-do-I-install-R-for-Windows_003f

says

If you want to be able to build packages from sources, we recommend that you
choose an installation path not containing spaces. (Using a path with spaces
in will probably work, but is little-tested.) Users of Vista/Windows
7/8/Server 2008/2012 installing for a single user using an account with
administrator rights1 should consider installing into a non-system area
(such as C:\R). Installing to a network share (a filepath starting with
\\machine\...) is not supported: such paths will need to mapped to a
network drive.

- Bob

On 11/24/13, 4:17 PM, Blaise Egan wrote:
> which also says I need to re-install R in a folder that does not have spaces in its path name. I don't like putting
> things outside of Program Files, but will do.
